scope: Salmon River, chiefly the Middle Fork and the Main Salmon: outfitter and guide credentials, water-specific operating areas, forest permit lists, the float permit, and one inspected launch
highest_priority_permission_question: Whether a result from the public license search is a public record that may be reused in a commercial directory. The privacy policy says personal information supplied for licensing is exempt and that other information may be inspected and copied. It does not state a commercial-directory grant. The search was opened only as a script shell, so the fields on a result were not seen.
method: Primary pages, the current outfitter rule PDF, and Idaho Code sections 36-2102, 36-2104, 36-2107, and 36-2108 were read on 2026-11-25. The license search returned a JavaScript shell and no roster. No account was used and no public-records request was sent. The forest outfitter lists were counted by collapsing a legal name and a DBA that share one website. Three Salmon River booking sites rendered. A membership PDF was not downloaded. A boat-renewal address returned a human-verification challenge. Operator URLs, personal names, and contact details are omitted from this file.

license_lookup.population: Public roster of outfitter and guide licensees. The board page links a search. The static response is a script shell and does not publish a roster. A special-authorization waitlist on the board page is not that roster.

sample.population: Salmon River bookable sample drawn from the forest's dated permit lists: three operator identities and one vessel row with no named hull. The 2023 Middle Fork list collapses to 27 website identities. The 2023 SA6 list collapses to 29. The undated SA5 list and the 2022 jet-boat list are the same 8 addresses. Those list sizes are not current license counts.

access_sites.population: Boundary Creek, the Middle Fork launch described by the Salmon-Challis National Forest. No Salmon River ramp census was taken.
access_sites.supported_identity: Boundary Creek boat launch on the Middle Fork of the Salmon, adjacent to the forest campground. This is not a license.

boat_records.population: Public hull or motorboat-certificate lookup. The boating page links renewal to a separate address that returned a human-verification challenge. No certificate was requested. Title 67, Chapter 70 was not read.

sources.field_scope: Section 36-2102, text marked effective until July 1, 2028. Defines outfitter, guide, board, and a license year of April 1 through March 31. A second text marked effective July 1, 2028 is on the page and was not compared.
Section 36-2104. Acting as an outfitter or guide without a license is a misdemeanor. Paying a person for those services while knowing the person is unlicensed is also a misdemeanor.
Section 36-2107. The board examines applicants, issues licenses with restrictions, and may cooperate with federal and state agencies on outfitting and guiding.

Section 36-2108, text marked effective until July 1, 2028. An outfitter application must include a worded description of the operating-area boundaries and is filed with a bond. The application was not filed.
sources.request_process: Application to the board. Not used.

sources.publisher: Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses
sources.field_scope: IDAPA 24.35.01, 22 pages, read for authority, definitions, license renewal, boat identification, and Salmon River section limits. The authority line cites Title 39, Chapter 21, dated July 1, 2026. The Act is defined as Title 36, Chapter 21. Rule 206 requires outfitter letters on a boat and limits the Clearwater sticker to sections CL2 and CL3. Rule 259 states MF1 as Boundary Creek to Cache Bar, float maximum 27 and power maximum none. SA5 and SA6 are stated. The section tables do not name holders.

sources.field_scope: A permit is required year round from Dagger Falls to the confluence with the Main Salmon. At most seven float parties, commercial and noncommercial, may launch per day. Recreation.gov handles reservations. The control-season lottery is described for private boating permits. A reservation is not the permit. Required boat equipment includes an Idaho invasive-species sticker as applicable. Boundary Creek is described as a launch.
sources.request_process: Reservations through Recreation.gov. No reservation was made.
